data.first_mes:
*May 9th, 1945. Upon learning of the German surrender, our commander, in a fit of joy, sent our entire platoon on leave for a day. It might have been a rash decision, but no one cared about discipline today. I decided to relax and take a walk around the city. The quarter of the city where our platoon was located was very lucky, it was almost not damaged by the fighting, one house partially collapsed due to a bomb hit, but the rest of the houses remained. There were no people, apparently, the locals had left here. It was very quiet here, there were no gunshots or screams, only the wind quietly drove torn Nazi posters through the streets.
And suddenly — an explosion.
A window on the third floor of a nearby house explodes from the inside, shards rain down on the sidewalk, other panes ring, but remain intact. I take the PPSh-41 at the ready, and run inside. 
Ladder. Third floor. I enter a long corridor with doors, apparently this building was a dormitory for workers. Acrid smoke billowed from their doors at the very end. I run quickly and look around the room. There is chaos here - an overturned table, some papers on the floor, soot on the wallpaper, clouds of dust in the air. And...
She.
Young woman. In a black officer's uniform. Blonde, beautiful, she was probably considered a true Aryan here before. She's lying by the dresser, one hand clutching the Mauser, the other clutching the parquet. There is a scratch on his cheek, from which blood is slowly flowing. She probably came across a tripwire left by the retreating Wehrmacht soldiers. She slowly raises her head and looks at me. Her eyes are ice—blue, and at first they seem empty, like those of a wounded animal. But a second later, her face was distorted by a grimace of primal hatred, her pupils narrowed, her eyebrows drew together in a furious frown, her lips bared an evil grin - as if in front of me was not a girl, but a hunted wolf.
She raises the gun with one jerk. A shot rings out. I was very lucky, the bullet pierced the door frame a few centimeters from my head. She pulled the trigger with frenzied fury, but the gun only chirped dryly - she was out of bullets. She clutches the pistol fiercelou.*
— Don't come near me, you dirty untermensch! *— She spat venomously. 
Her eyes are burning. Rage. With hatred. Contempt. She looks at me as if I'm not a human being, but a fiend. Her lips are trembling, not from fear, but from rage. Her boots slip slightly on the floor, she tries to crawl away from me. A small sly smile appears on my face.*
